chunks: Remember when We took your pledge and exalted you on the Mount (saying:) "Hold fast to what We have given you, firmly, and pay heed," you said: "We have heard and will not obey." (The image of) the calf had sunk deep into their hearts on account of unbelief. Say: "Vile is your belief if you are believers indeed!"

key_terms.سَمِعْنَا وَ عَصَيْنَا: "We heard and disobeyed" (a specific phrase used by the Israelites)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the phrase 'We heard and disobeyed' in the context of the Children of Israel?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the phrase 'We heard and disobeyed' (Sami'na wa 'asayna) is often contrasted with the faithful response 'We hear and obey' (Sami'na wa ata'na) to highlight the spiritual deficiency of the Israelites. The 'drinking of the calf into their hearts' signifies a deep-seated idolatry of the self and material desires, a theme central to the concept of *Kufr* in Alid theology. This verse serves as a cautionary archetype for the Ummah, illustrating how superficial adherence to divine law can mask a core of disbelief.
